description: DukascopyAdapter.fetch does not translate a transport-raised third-party exception into a returned refusal; it delegates all network-failure translation to the injected transport and wraps no transport call in try/except (dukascopy.py:605). Payload-parse faults (lzma.LZMAError, struct) ARE caught and translated; transport-level network/OS exceptions are not. 7 parametrized exception types all escape.
expected: CT-15 invariant: a boundary failure (transient venue failure / unavailable dependency) is RETURNED as a typed CT-04 refusal, never raised across the CT-15 boundary (DEC-0109).
observed: Real third-party exceptions (ConnectionResetError, ConnectionError, socket.timeout/TimeoutError, OSError, BrokenPipeError, urllib.error.URLError) escape DukascopyAdapter.fetch instead of surfacing as a returned refusal.

description: ExternalSourceIngest.fetch_and_intake calls self._port.fetch(request) with no try/except (ingest.py:445), so a provider port that raises propagates out of the middleware-to-application boundary. Same root cause as E6-F01/F02 (the real adapters ARE the ports and raise when their transport raises). The ExternalSourcePort protocol nominally returns Result, so this is the transitive manifestation / a missing defense-in-depth guard at the ingest seam.
expected: CT-15 invariant: no exception type escapes the CT-15 boundary; every provider fault surfaces as a returned CT-04 refusal (transient venue failure | unavailable dependency | invalid input | storage failure).
observed: A ConnectionResetError raised by the injected port escapes ExternalSourceIngest.fetch_and_intake instead of surfacing as a returned refusal.

description: PLAN L1-006 'never resolves a path outside the immutable raw-archive root' has no attackable surface in Epic 6: the Dukascopy adapter never builds a filesystem path from provider input (symbols are opaque instrument-map keys / native-id text; the byte transport is injected). The nearest real surface — a hostile provider symbol — is tested clean across 15 adversarial cases (all refuse, none raise). The raw-archive path-safety clause itself is Epic-3 store territory; recorded UNPROVEN-here (narrowed), not a defect.
expected: Filesystem path-traversal safety is provable where an archive path is resolved from input (Epic 3 CT-11 store); the intake seam exposes no such surface, so its hostile-identifier obligation (refuse, never resolve a path) is proven instead — and passes.
